_about: T-416 HOLIDAYS (decided by the user 2026-10-17/18): the single source for the game's holiday table and the companion's. Read by tools/genholidays.py, which writes engineGba/src/data/daemons_holidays.h (and the flags, VAR and constants) with --write, and prints the companion's server/data/holidays.json with --companion. Approved table: docs/private/draft-holidays-2026-10-17.md. Three a month: one COMMON to both editions, one for CONTENT (northern), one for CONTEXT (southern). In-world names in the game, real names only in the companion.
draft: EVERY IN-GAME WORD HERE IS DRAFT until the user approves it on the field page: the holiday names, the givers' lines, THE YEAR's section name, titles and lines. The givers' lines and THE YEAR's arrival line are approved as DRAFTs (the user, 2026-10-18).

rules.easter: offset in days from Easter Sunday (the Gregorian computus; the game holds a table for 2024-2040, written by tools/genholidays.py)
rules.table: one date a year, 'MM-DD' by year (the Mid-Autumn Festival: the 15th of the 8th lunar month, as published)
rules.season_start: the day the edition's own season begins (tools/seasons.py: north winter 12-21, spring 3-21, summer 6-21, autumn 9-22; CONTEXT's year two seasons on)
rules.days: how long from the start, in days. With no clock (play time) every holiday lasts ONE WATCH (15 minutes of play) -- the user, 2026-10-17
rules.eve_from_hour: begins at that hour of the day before (ROLLOVER at dusk on Dec 31)
rules.banner_watches: the watches the banner names it in (default all)
rules.play_watch: with no clock, which kind of watch it is snapped to in the play-time year (default: the nearest)
rules.two_on_one_day: the edition's holiday shows; the COMMON one's gift still waits at the CHECKPOINT (the user, 2026-10-17)
rules.steps_off: names a COMMON holiday this one is not on the day of: that day is the other's, and this one goes on the next day, inside its own span (SCIENCE FAIR off FLEDGLING DAY, the user, 2026-10-18)
rules.gift: a list read in order; an entry whose 'when' matches gives and stops, unless 'go_on'. give: an item name, {line: id} (a line for THE YEAR, once ever), {lead_type_gain} (the party lead's GAIN item, by its first type; a lead that is ORACLE as EITHER type reads on to the next entry -- the user, 2026-10-18) or {year_draw: [items]} (one by the year and the edition). when: watches, sky (CLEAR RAIN STORM SNOW FOG WIND), weekdays, storm_on_islands_today. ITEMS once per holiday per year (a flag each, and a VAR holding the year); LINES once ever.
rules.daemons: a holiday takes a land slot -- the road's SEASON slot by default (tools/gbashifts.py), 'hour' its HOUR slot, or a number -- or a fishing slot ('fish'), keeping its level and odds; it wins over the season row on that slot for the day. 'A|B' names are CONTENT's | CONTEXT's. Never a gate: each is met in the wild somewhere already.

months_about: Each month a note of the chromatic scale, C (JAN) to B (DEC), in the user's colours; A is INDIGO (the user, 2026-10-17). 'rgb5' is the muted UI colour the banner's mark, the trainer card and the holiday banner wear (9.4: 22+ CIE76 from every type hue; naturals are the weekday trims exactly); 'key_colour_index' is the bright PLAY palette slot (PALTAG_KEY_COLOURS, tools/genplaynotes.py) the fireworks draw in. NOV moved from the draft's 11,6,18 (9 from OCT) to 9,3,19 -- kept by the user 2026-10-18, DRAFT.

play_time.about: With no clock (vision 9.21, T-273): an hour of play is a day for the watches, seven hours a season, so the play-time year is 28 hours and starts at the northern June 21 (CONTEXT meets it as its winter). A holiday holds the one watch its date falls in (snapped to the kind of watch it needs); a moving holiday sits on its mean date, 2024-2040.

lines.title: ROLLOVER
lines.text: The count ran out and began again. Nothing I learned was kept in the number.

lines.title: EVEN LIGHT, SPRING
lines.text: Day and night came out even. From here the light is the one that grows.

lines.title: EVEN LIGHT, AUTUMN
lines.text: Day and night came out even. From here the dark has its turn, and that is fair.

lines.title: DAWN VIGIL
lines.text: Others kept watch so this morning could be ordinary. I keep a minute of it for them.

lines.title: FIRST FROST
lines.text: The first frost says nothing new. It only says it clearly.

lines.title: DEN DAY
lines.text: It brought nothing home. It was already looking ahead for me.
lines.about: DEN DAY with a lead that is ORACLE as either type (no daemon is ORACLE first; OLD_UNOWN_B is ORACLE second), which has no GAIN item (the user, 2026-10-18)

lines.title: FLEDGLING DAY
lines.text: Everyone I met was new at this once. The best of them still say so.

lines.title: LANTERN NIGHTS
lines.text: A light left in the window is not for me. I leave it on anyway.

lines.title: SCIENCE FAIR
lines.text: The result I wanted and the result I got sat side by side. I wrote down the second.

lines.title: TRUCE DAY
lines.text: Nobody won today. Everyone went home. That was the whole of it.

lines.title: MARIGOLD DAYS
lines.text: Said out loud, they stay in the story. I said the names I have.

lines.title: GIVING THANKS
lines.text: I counted what I had. It came to more than I carried in.

routine_looks_about: T-392 P3 (the user, 2026-10-18): on a holiday a routine's SIGNATURE takes its look -- never its daemon, never its picture underneath. Colours ONLY from the twelve month colours (PLAY's bright key colours, PALTAG_KEY_COLOURS): a month name, MONTH (the holiday's own), ALL (the twelve, one glyph each), or a #hex read as the NEAREST month by hue (Christmas's red and green read as JAN and JUN; pastels and gold read as the nearest month). BLACK is the glyph filled with the outline's own true black, ringed in the first colour (DRAFT). 'bleach' (white, silver, frost: no hue, so no month) wears the type's own ink paled, as LEGACY's is -- no colour added (DRAFT). shape: KEEP (the routine's own path), RING (a burst outward), HEART (the glyphs placed as a heart -- of bits, never vanilla's heart sprite), STARS (held points that twinkle), SCATTER, SWEEP, FALL, ORBIT (round the target). 'notes': every glyph a note. 'twinkle': the glyphs blink. A QUIET holiday dresses no routine: its signatures keep their ink and play soft. tools/genholidays.py writes sHolidayRoutineLooks; tools/gensignature.py draws the lane sheet. Every look DRAFT.
